label: ass:coeff
title: Assumption
body_md:
\label{ass:coeff}
There are fixed global event times $0=\theta_0<\theta_1<\cdots<\theta_{N_{\rm ev}}<T=\theta_{N_{\rm ev}+1}$. On each $I_j=(\theta_j,\theta_{j+1})$, $s,b,\gamma$ are elementwise constant in space and belong to $W^{1,\infty}(I_j)$ on each element. Their one-sided limits exist at events and
\[
 0<s_*\le s\le s^*,\qquad 0<b_*\le b\le b^*,\qquad 0\le\gamma\le\gamma^*.
\]
The mesh resolves fixed spatial material interfaces. The spatial mesh is unchanged at temporal events. Integrals are evaluated exactly, or with quadrature exact for the polynomial products appearing in the scheme.
head: environment

label: prop:balance
title: Proposition
head: environment
name: Continuous balances

title: Proof
body_md: For model 1, differentiating the material energy and substituting \eqref{eq:m1} gives $(\mathbf{E},\mathbf{J})-\mathcal L_1+\mathcal W_1$. For model 2, its material derivative gives $(\mathbf{E},s\mathbf{V})-\mathcal L_2$ plus the differentiated weights, whereas \eqref{eq:poynting} equals $-(\mathbf{E},s\mathbf{V}+(\partial_t s)\mathbf{Q})$. For model 3 the electromagnetic contribution is $-(\mathbf{E},s\mathbf{V})$, with no $(\partial_t s)\mathbf{Q}$ term because $\mathbf{P}$ is independent. For model 4, the two oscillator coupling terms $-(b/\epsilon_0)\mathbf{P}\cdot \mathbf{V}$ and $(b/\epsilon_0)\mathbf{P}\cdot \mathbf{V}$ cancel. This proves all four identities.
head: environment

label: thm:semi
title: Theorem
head: environment
name: Semidiscrete energy balance

title: Proof
body_md:
Choose $\mathbf{v}=\mathbf{E}_h$, $\mathbf{w}=\mathbf{H}_h$, and $\widehat{\mathbf{v}}=\widehat{\mathbf{E}}_h$ in \eqref{eq:hdg-eqs}. The element curl integration identity gives the combined boundary term
\[
 \left\langle\mathbf{n}\times \mathbf{H}_h,\mathbf{E}_h-\widehat{\mathbf{E}}_h\right\rangle_{\partial\mathcal T_h}
 -\left\langle\mathbf{n}\times\widehat{\mathbf{H}}_h,\mathbf{E}_h\right\rangle_{\partial\mathcal T_h}
 =\left\langle\mathbf{n}\times \mathbf{H}_h-\mathbf{n}\times\widehat{\mathbf{H}}_h,\mathbf{E}_h-\widehat{\mathbf{E}}_h\right\rangle_{\partial\mathcal T_h}
 =\mathcal D_h,
\]
where the conservativity equation \eqref{eq:hdg3}, namely $\left\langle\mathbf{n}\times\widehat{\mathbf{H}}_h,\widehat{\mathbf{v}}\right\rangle_{\partial\mathcal T_h}=0$ for all $\widehat{\mathbf{v}}\in M_h^0$, was used to subtract the trace from the second pairing. Hence
\[
 \partial_t\mathcal E_{{\rm em},h}+\mathcal D_h=-(\partial_t\mathbf{P}_h,\mathbf{E}_h).
\]
The material cancellation is the same as in Proposition~\ref{prop:balance}. The element-wise coefficient assumption makes every required weighted test admissible. State transfer gives the event identities. Finally, $\mathcal W_{i,h}\le C_i\mathcal E_{i,h}$ and $\mathcal L_{i,h},\mathcal D_h\ge0$ imply the bound by interval-wise integration and event multiplication.
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md:
Theorem~\ref{thm:semi} controls $\mathbf{E}_h,\mathbf{H}_h,\mathbf{Q}_h,\mathbf{V}_h$ but not $\mathbf{P}_h$ alone. The independent equation gives
\[
 \left\|\mathbf{P}_h(t)\right\|\le\left\|\mathbf{P}_h(0)\right\|+s^*\int_0^t\left\|\mathbf{V}_h(r)\right\|dr
 \le\left\|\mathbf{P}_h(0)\right\|+C T\sqrt{G_3(T)\mathcal E_{3,h}(0)}.
\]
Then $\mathbf{D}_h=\epsilon_0 \mathbf{E}_h+\mathbf{P}_h$ is controlled. This is preferable to describing the physical energy as coercive on all five states.
head: environment
name: The additional state in model 3

label: ass:solution
title: Assumption
body_md:
\label{ass:solution}
On every event-free interval $I_j$, each continuous state belongs to $W^{1,1}(I_j;L^2(\Omega))$ and has one-sided endpoint values. The states satisfy the model equations and the exact temporal transmission rules. Electric and magnetic tangential traces are single-valued across interior and paired periodic facets; the electric trace vanishes on PEC facets, also at one-sided event limits. For variant B, $\mathbf{H}$ is uniformly in broken $\mathbf{H}^{k+1}$ and $\mathbf{E}$ and every independent material state are uniformly in broken $\mathbf{H}^{k+2}$ on each closed slab: the quantities $\mathcal A_i,\mathcal B$ defined below are finite, uniformly over refinement of a fixed mesh-resolved material partition. For variant A, all these fields instead have uniformly bounded broken $\mathbf{H}^{k+1}$ norms. Additional temporal derivatives required by a time-discrete estimate are stated in that estimate.
head: environment
name: Solution regularity and transmission

label: lem:compat
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Exact projection compatibility

title: Proof
body_md:
Each material equation is a linear combination of electric/material states with scalar coefficients constant on $K$. Applying $\Pi_E$ therefore gives exactly the discrete material equation. No common projection of $\mathbf{E}$ and $\mathbf{H}$ is needed for this step.

Mass projection defects vanish against the corresponding volume tests. Furthermore,
\[
 \nabla\times W_h^E\subset W_h^H,\qquad \nabla\times W_h^H\subset W_h^E,
\]
for $m=k$ or $m=k+1$. Thus $(\mathbf{e}_H^I,\nabla\times \mathbf{v})_K=(\mathbf{e}_E^I,\nabla\times \mathbf{w})_K=0$. The tangential trace of $\mathbf{w}$ has degree at most $k\le m$, so $\langle \mathbf{n}\times\mathbf{e}_{E_T}^I,\mathbf{w}\rangle_{\partial K}=0$ by facet projection orthogonality. The projected magnetic numerical flux differs from $\mathbf{n}\times \mathbf{H}$ by exactly $R_K$. Subtracting the discrete equations from these projected equations proves \eqref{eq:erra}--\eqref{eq:errflux}. Interior exact magnetic fluxes cancel against single-valued hybrid tests.
head: environment

label: lem:errorenergy
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Projected-error energy identity

title: Proof
body_md: Test \eqref{eq:erra} with $\mathbf{e}_E^h$ and \eqref{eq:errf} with $\mathbf{e}_H^h$. In the boundary cancellation the nonzero conservativity residual \eqref{eq:errc}, tested with $\widehat{\mathbf{e}}_{E_T}^h$, contributes $+\langle R,\widehat{\mathbf{e}}_{E_T}^h\rangle$ to the right-hand side. Thus the boundary forcing is precisely $-\langle R,\mathbf{e}_{E,T}^h-\widehat{\mathbf{e}}_{E_T}^h\rangle$. Material energy cancellation is exact by Lemma~\ref{lem:compat}. Weighted Cauchy--Schwarz bounds this forcing by $F_h\mathcal D_h(\mathbf{e}_i^h)^{1/2}$, and Young's inequality gives \eqref{eq:errineq}.
head: environment

label: prop:resrates
title: Proposition
head: environment
name: Residual rates

title: Proof
body_md: Insert each degree and stabilization choice into \eqref{eq:resgeneric}. In variant B the magnetic contribution gains a factor $h_K$ from $\tau_K^{-1}$, while the electric contribution loses a factor $h_K$ but starts with the higher-degree trace estimate. Both powers become $h_K^{2k+2}$.
head: environment

label: lem:integrated
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Energy estimate including all events

title: Proof
body_md:
On smooth intervals multiply \eqref{eq:errineq} by
\[
 w_i(t)=\exp\!\left(-\int_0^t C_i(r)dr\right)
 \prod_{\theta_j\le t}\max\{1,\rho_{i,j}\}^{-1}.
\]
The weighted energy has a nonpositive jump at each event. Integrating gives
\[
 w_i(t)\mathcal E_i(\mathbf{e}_i^h(t))+\tfrac12\int_0^t w_i\mathcal D_h(\mathbf{e}_i^h)dr
 \le \mathcal E_i(\mathbf{e}_i^h(0))+\tfrac12\int_0^t w_i F_h^2dr.
\]
Since $G_i(T)^{-1}\le w_i\le1$, the stated estimate follows (with an absolute constant accounting for the sum of the supremum and dissipation).
head: environment

label: thm:error
title: Theorem
head: environment
name: Common $h^{k+1}$ rate for variant B

title: Proof
body_md:
Combine \eqref{eq:resB} and Lemma~\ref{lem:integrated}. The physical quadratic energy is uniformly equivalent to the indicated $L^2$ state norm for models 1, 2, and 4. Add the projection approximation: it is $O(h^{k+1})$ for $\mathbf{H}$ and $O(h^{k+2})$ for the degree-$(k+1)$ electric/material states. The energy error is $O(h^{k+1})$, so it limits the common rate.

For model 3 use the reduced physical energy. Its independent projected polarization satisfies
\[
 \partial_t\mathbf{e}_P^h=s \mathbf{e}_V^h,\qquad \mathbf{e}_P^h(0)=0,
\]
including continuity at all events. Thus $\sup_t\left\|\mathbf{e}_P^h(t)\right\|\le s^*T\sup_t\left\|\mathbf{e}_V^h(t)\right\|$. Add the projection error for $\mathbf{P}$ and use $\mathbf{D}=\epsilon_0 \mathbf{E}+\mathbf{P}$. This proves both the full-state rate and the dissipation bound.
head: environment

label: cor:baseline
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:baseline}
Variant A, with projected initial data and the corresponding broken $\mathbf{H}^{k+1}$ regularity, satisfies the analogous common-state estimate of order $h^{k+1/2}$. It follows from \eqref{eq:resA} and Lemma~\ref{lem:integrated}. Theorem~\ref{thm:error} does not upgrade variant A to order $h^{k+1}$.
head: environment
name: The equal-degree variant A

label: rem:compatible
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:compatible}
The regularity and spatial transmission assumptions are hypotheses about the exact solution, not consequences of bounded piecewise smooth coefficients. In particular, a spatially heterogeneous model-2 event can produce an electric jump whose tangential values are incompatible across a material interface. Here $\Delta s:=s^+-s^-$ denotes the change in the coupling coefficient across the event. Indeed, since $\mathbf{E}^+-\mathbf{E}^-=-(\Delta s)\mathbf{Q}/\epsilon_0$, preservation of a continuous pre-event tangential electric trace requires
\[
 \mathopen{[\![}(\Delta s)\mathbf{Q}\mathclose{]\!]}_T=0
 \quad\hbox{on internal material interfaces},\qquad
 \mathbf{n}\times((\Delta s)\mathbf{Q})=0\quad\hbox{on PEC boundaries}.
\]
Here $\mathopen{[\![}\cdot\mathclose{]\!]}_T$ denotes a spatial tangential jump, distinct from the temporal jump $\left[\cdot\right]$. These are necessary trace compatibility conditions, not sufficient conditions for higher broken Sobolev regularity. Incompatible data may fail Assumption~\ref{ass:solution}. The theorem applies to compatible switching histories; lower regularity requires appropriately reduced approximation estimates. None of the constants is claimed uniform in the zero-coupling or zero-resonance limit.
head: environment
name: Regularity at heterogeneous switching events

label: prop:be
title: Proposition
head: environment
name: Discrete energy stability of both methods

title: Proof
body_md:
Pair each discrete equation with $Z_n$ in the frozen energy inner product. The semidiscrete cancellation \eqref{eq:frozen} gives dissipation and material loss. The identity
\[
 (Y_h^n-Y_h^{n-1},Z_n)_{\mathsf G_n^*}
 =\mathcal E_n^*(Y_h^n)-\mathcal E_n^*(Y_h^{n-1})
 +\sigma\left\|Y_h^n-Y_h^{n-1}\right\|_{\mathsf G_n^*}^2
\]
proves \eqref{eq:commonenergy}. Applied to the homogeneous step with zero incoming state, it makes the outgoing state zero. The finite-dimensional square system is therefore invertible. To pass between frozen metrics, compare the unchanged state in successive $\mathsf G_n^*$; on a smooth slab the comparison is bounded by $\exp(\int C_i)$, and at an event by $\rho_{i,j}$. The smooth comparison intervals have disjoint interiors within each slab, so their total exponent is bounded by the slab integral in \eqref{eq:G}; a comparison crossing an event is split into two smooth pieces and its event factor. State transfer itself is the identity. This proves \eqref{eq:discretestability}. For model 3, subtract the polarization equation from the displacement equation to obtain a closed reduced system, apply the same calculation to its coercive energy, and then sum $\mathbf{P}_h^n-\mathbf{P}_h^{n-1}=\Delta t_n s(t_n^*)\mathbf{V}_h^n$ for backward Euler or $\Delta t_n s(t_n^*)\overline{\mathbf{V}}_h^n$ for midpoint.
head: environment

label: thm:full
title: Theorem
head: environment
name: Fully discrete common-state convergence

title: Proof
body_md:
Set $e_i^{h,n}=\Pi_iY_i(t_n)-Y_{i,h}^n$ and $\widehat{\mathbf{e}}_{E_T}^{h,n}=\Pi_M \mathbf{E}_T(t_n)-\widehat{\mathbf{E}}_h^n$. Projection commutes with backward differences because the spatial operators are fixed. Lemma~\ref{lem:compat} therefore gives the same spatial residual $R^n$, plus the volume time defects $g_{i,n}$ in all differential state equations. No discrete inverse estimate enters this argument.

Testing these equations in the frozen physical energy and using the polarization identity gives
\begin{align}\label{eq:fullerridentity}
 \mathcal E_i^n(e_i^{h,n})&+\tfrac12\left\|e_i^{h,n}-e_i^{h,n-1}\right\|_{\mathsf G_i^n}^2
 +\Delta t_n(\mathcal D_h(e^n)+\mathcal L_i^n(e^n))\\
 &=\mathcal E_i^n(e_i^{h,n-1})
 -\Delta t_n\sum_K\langle R_K^n,\mathbf{e}_{E,T}^{h,n}-\widehat{\mathbf{e}}_{E_T}^{h,n}\rangle_{\partial K}
 +\Delta t_n(e_i^{h,n},g_{i,n})_{\mathsf G_i^n}.\nonumber
\end{align}
The facet term is bounded by $\tfrac12\Delta t_n(\mathcal D_h(e^n)+(F_h^n)^2)$. Keep the time-defect term linear in the error norm:
\[
 |(e_i^{h,n},g_{i,n})_{\mathsf G_i^n}|
 \le\left\|e_i^{h,n}\right\|_{\mathsf G_i^n}\left\|g_{i,n}\right\|_{\mathsf G_i^n}.
\]
For each step, let $r_n$ compare the energy of the unchanged preceding error in the current frozen metric with its preceding endpoint energy. Include a zero-length comparison step at each event, with $r_n=\rho_{i,j}$ and unchanged continuous error. Set $R_0=1$, $R_n=\prod_{\ell=1}^n\max\{1,r_\ell\}$, and $w_n=R_n^{-1}$. The smooth-slab comparison and event identities give $1\le R_n\le G_i(T)$. Also $w_n\mathcal E_i^n(e_i^{h,n-1})\le w_{n-1}\mathcal E_i^{n-1}(e_i^{h,n-1})$, with the analogous inequality at an event. Dropping nonnegative dissipation and increment terms, summing through index $m$, and multiplying by two gives
\[
 w_m\left\|e_i^m\right\|_{M_i^m}^2
 \le\left\|e_i^0\right\|_{M_i^0}^2
   +\sum_{n=1}^m\Delta t_n w_n(F_h^n)^2
   +2\sum_{n=1}^m\Delta t_n w_n
       \left\|e_i^{h,n}\right\|_{\mathsf G_i^n}\left\|g_{i,n}\right\|_{\mathsf G_i^n}.
\]
Let $U_m=\max_{0\le n\le m}\sqrt{w_n}\left\|e_i^{h,n}\right\|_{\mathsf G_i^n}$, and apply the preceding inequality at an index realizing this maximum. Writing
\[
 A_m^2=\left\|e_i^0\right\|_{M_i^0}^2+\sum_{n=1}^m\Delta t_n w_n(F_h^n)^2,
 \qquad B_m=\sum_{n=1}^m\Delta t_n\sqrt{w_n}\left\|g_{i,n}\right\|_{\mathsf G_i^n},
\]
we obtain $U_m^2\le A_m^2+2U_mB_m$, hence $U_m\le A_m+2B_m$. Consequently,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:fullprojectedbound}
 \max_n\left\|e_i^{h,n}\right\|_{\mathsf G_i^n}
 \le G_i(T)^{1/2}\left[\left\|e_i^0\right\|_{M_i^0}
       +\left(\sum_n\Delta t_n(F_h^n)^2\right)^{1/2}
       +2\sum_n\Delta t_n\left\|g_{i,n}\right\|_{\mathsf G_i^n}\right].
\end{equation}
The projected initial error vanishes. By \eqref{eq:resB}, the spatial term is at most $C\sqrt T h^{k+1}\mathcal S$; by \eqref{eq:defectbound}, the time term is at most $CT\Delta t_{\max}\mathcal T_i$. Add the nodal projection error and use uniform energy equivalence to obtain \eqref{eq:fullrate}. No discrete Gronwall estimate is needed.
head: environment

label: cor:full3
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:full3}
For variant B in model 3 the same common space--time rate holds for $(\mathbf{E},\mathbf{H},\mathbf{Q},\mathbf{V})$ if the reduced exact state $X_3=(\mathbf{E},\mathbf{H},\mathbf{Q},\mathbf{V})$ is piecewise $W^{2,\infty}(I_j;L^2)$ and satisfies the spatial assumptions. It extends to $\mathbf{P},\mathbf{D}$ if $\mathbf{P}$ has the corresponding spatial approximation regularity and is piecewise $W^{2,\infty}(I_j;L^2)$.
head: environment
name: Model 3

title: Proof
body_md:
Subtracting the backward Euler polarization equation from its displacement equation gives, exactly,
\[
 \epsilon_0\frac{\mathbf{E}_h^n-\mathbf{E}_h^{n-1}}{\Delta t_n}
       -\nabla\times_h \mathbf{H}_h^n+s^nV_h^n=0
\]
in the HDG weak form. Thus the reduced variables form a closed system with the coercive energy \eqref{eq:energy3}; the preceding projected-exact-solution argument applies to that system. Its electric equation has no $\partial_t s$ term, because $\mathbf{P}$ is an independent state. Finally the full polarization error satisfies
\[
 \mathbf{e}_P^{h,n}-\mathbf{e}_P^{h,n-1}=\Delta t_n(s^n \mathbf{e}_V^{h,n}+\Pi_E d_{\mathbf{P},n}),
\]
with zero initial error and unchanged event states. Summing and applying \eqref{eq:defectbound} gives
\[
 \max_n\left\|\mathbf{e}_P^{h,n}\right\|\le s^*T\max_n\left\|\mathbf{e}_V^{h,n}\right\|
       +CT\Delta t_{\max}\max_j\left\|\partial_t^2\mathbf{P}\right\|_{L^\infty(I_j;L^2)}.
\]
Add the projection error and reconstruct $\mathbf{D}=\epsilon_0 \mathbf{E}+\mathbf{P}$.
head: environment

label: thm:midfull
title: Theorem
head: environment
name: Fixed-mesh fully discrete midpoint estimate

title: Proof
body_md:
For an event-free step put $a=t_{n-1/2}$ and let $\bar Y_{i,h}(t_n)=\tfrac12(Y_{i,h}(t_n)+Y_{i,h}(t_{n-1}))$. The exact semidiscrete state has the midpoint defect
\[
 d_n^{\rm mid}=\frac{Y_{i,h}(t_n)-Y_{i,h}(t_{n-1})}{\Delta t_n}
                  -A_{i,h}(a)\bar Y_{i,h}(t_n).
\]
Since $\partial_tY_{i,h}(a)=A_{i,h}(a)Y_{i,h}(a)$, centered Taylor estimates give
\[
 \left\|d_n^{\rm mid}\right\|_{M_h(a)}
 \le C\Delta t_n^2\mathcal T_{i,h}^{\rm mid}.
\]
Indeed the centered difference of $Y_{i,h}$ differs from $\partial_tY_{i,h}(a)$ by $O(\Delta t_n^2\partial_t^3Y_{i,h})$, while $\bar Y_{i,h}(t_n)-Y_{i,h}(a)=O(\Delta t_n^2\partial_t^2Y_{i,h})$ in the graph norm of $A_{i,h}(a)$.
The exact and discrete equations evaluate the same coefficients at $a$; their time variation is thus included in these temporal and graph-norm regularity quantities, while the varying energy weight is handled by the metric comparisons below.

Set $e^n=Y_{i,h}(t_n)-Y_{i,h}^n$. Subtract the two midpoint equations, test with $\bar e^n=(e^n+e^{n-1})/2$ in the frozen energy, and use \eqref{eq:frozen}:
\begin{equation}\label{eq:miderrorenergy}
 \mathcal E_n^*(e^n)-\mathcal E_n^*(e^{n-1})
 +\Delta t_n\bigl(\mathcal D_h(\bar e^n;a)+\mathcal L_h(\bar e^n;a)\bigr)
 =\Delta t_n(\bar e^n,d_n^{\rm mid})_{M_h(a)}.
\end{equation}
Let $r_n$ compare consecutive frozen energy metrics, including a zero-length comparison at every event, and set $w_n=\prod_{\ell\le n}\max\{1,r_\ell\}^{-1}$. As in the backward Euler energy estimate above, $G_i(T)^{-1}\le w_n\le1$. Multiplying \eqref{eq:miderrorenergy} by $w_n$, summing, and setting $U_m=\max_{n\le m}\sqrt{w_n}\left\|e^n\right\|_{\mathsf G_n^*}$ yields
\[
 U_m^2\le 2U_m\sum_{n\le m}\Delta t_n\sqrt{w_n}\left\|d_n^{\rm mid}\right\|_{\mathsf G_n^*}.
\]
Here the incoming half of $\bar e^n$ is bounded in the current metric by the preceding weighted energy. Thus $\max_n\left\|e^n\right\|_{\mathsf G_n^*}\le C G_i(T)^{1/2}T\Delta t^2\mathcal T_{i,h}^{\rm mid}$. Add the semidiscrete spatial estimate \eqref{eq:spatialerror}. For model 3 the same energy argument applies to the reduced state; summing the polarization midpoint error equation bounds $\mathbf P$, and $\mathbf D=\epsilon_0\mathbf E+\mathbf P$ then follows.
head: environment

label: cor:forced
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:forced}
Under the respective regularity assumptions, the spatial estimates of Theorem~\ref{thm:error} and Corollary~\ref{cor:baseline}, the backward Euler estimates of Theorem~\ref{thm:full} and Corollary~\ref{cor:full3}, and the midpoint estimate of Theorem~\ref{thm:midfull} hold for \eqref{eq:forced} with exact Galerkin loads. Backward Euler evaluates $\Pi_iF_i$ at the appropriate one-sided endpoint; midpoint evaluates it at the step midpoint. The stability identity \eqref{eq:commonenergy} gains the corresponding source-work term.
head: environment
name: Exact Galerkin loads

title: Proof
body_md: Projection of the continuous forced equations produces exactly the discrete load. Subtraction cancels the source in the spatial error equation and leaves the same temporal defects. For midpoint, the source at the slab midpoint also cancels when the exact semidiscrete equation is evaluated there. Model 3's polarization difference has the same cancellation. The homogeneous energy identity becomes a forced energy inequality through Cauchy--Schwarz on the source work.
head: environment

label: prop:timing
title: Proposition
head: environment
name: Error caused by displaced switches

title: Proof
body_md: Variation of constants for the difference of the two continuous states gives an integral supported only on the $W_j$. On $W_j$ its forcing is $\pm(A_{j-1}-A_j)Y$; the propagator bound and the interval length give \eqref{eq:timingbound}.
head: environment

label: rem:timinguniform
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:timinguniform}
The energy bounds give $C_U$ independently of $h$ under the stated coefficient assumptions. For models 1, 3, and 4, switching changes only bounded material terms, so their generator defects are controlled by the state norm. In model 2, $\mathbf{E}_s=(\mathbf{D}-s\mathbf{Q})/\epsilon_0$ determines the PEC domain of the frozen Maxwell operator. A sufficient condition for both one-sided reconstructions to belong to $H_0(
abla	imes;\Omega)$ is $(s^+-s^-)\mathbf{Q}(r)\in H_0(
abla	imes;\Omega)$ on each swept interval, together with admissibility of one reconstruction. Broken-curl $L^2$ bounds alone do not impose the required tangential continuity or PEC trace. The magnetic generator defect includes $
abla	imes((s^+-s^-)\mathbf{Q})/(\mu_0\epsilon_0)$, so full-state $L^2$ control does not itself give an $h$-uniform $B_j$. The claim for model 2 therefore requires the common-domain and uniform defect bounds; fixed bounded Fourier modes satisfy the finite-dimensional version.
head: environment
name: Which constants are uniform over an HDG mesh?

label: prop:midtiming
title: Proposition
head: environment
name: First variation and midpoint map error

title: Proof
body_md: Differentiating \eqref{eq:periodDL} gives $S'(\theta)=K(\theta)$. On a constant slab a midpoint step differs from its matrix exponential by $O(\Delta t_n^3)$; summing these defects gives $O(\Delta t^2)$. Taylor expansion in $\delta$ then yields the stated estimates.
head: environment

label: prop:sharpDL
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:sharpDL}
On a unit-volume periodic cell choose a fixed unit vector $\mathbf{u}$ and take spatially constant fields with $\mathbf{H}=0$. For model 1 with $\epsilon_0=\mu_0=1$, $b=1$, and $\gamma=0$, prescribe
\[
 \mathbf{D}(0)=\mathbf{u},\quad \mathbf{P}(0)=\mathbf{J}(0)=0,\quad
 s(t)=\begin{cases}1,&t<1/3,\\2,&t>1/3.\end{cases}
\]
Fix $T=1$, $\theta=1/3$, and uniform base grids with
\[
N_r=3\cdot2^r+1,\qquad \Delta t_r=1/N_r,\qquad
 \widetilde\theta_r=2^r\Delta t_r,\quad r\ge1.
\]
Since $N_r/3=2^r+1/3$, the selected grid node is the one with index $2^r$, and $\delta_r=\widetilde\theta_r-\theta=-\Delta t_r/3$. There are constants $c,C>0$, independent of $r$, such that for all sufficiently large $r$ each of the following final continuous-state errors lies between $c\Delta t_r$ and $C\Delta t_r$: the exact propagator on this displaced schedule, and midpoint with coefficients sampled at the base-step midpoints. Midpoint with the crossing step split at the exact switch has error $O(\Delta t_r^2)$. Both HDG variants represent this spatially constant evolution exactly in space, for every $k\ge0$.
head: environment
name: First-order switch-shifted-switch midpoint

label: eq:sharpA
title: Proof
body_md:
Write the scalar amplitudes in the $\mathbf{u}$ direction as
$\mathbf{D}=d\mathbf{u}$, $\mathbf{P}=p\mathbf{u}$,
$\mathbf{J}=j\mathbf{u}$, and $\mathbf{E}=e\mathbf{u}$.  The invariant
subsystem in $y=(d,p,j)^T$ is
\begin{equation}\label{eq:sharpA}
 \partial_t y=A(s)y,\qquad
 A(s)=\begin{pmatrix}0&0&0\\0&0&1\\s&-(s+1)&0\end{pmatrix},
 \quad y_0=(1,0,0)^T.
\end{equation}
Before the switch the scalar electric amplitude is $e(t)=\tfrac12(1+\cos(\sqrt2 t))$, so $e(\theta)>0$. Hence
\[
 (A_--A_+)y(\theta)=(0,0,-e(\theta))^T\ne0.
\]
The exponential $e^{(T-\theta)A_+}$ is invertible, so $v=K(\theta)y_0\ne0$. Thus
\[
 y_{\rm rnd}^{\rm exact}(T)-y(T)=\delta_r v+O(\Delta t_r^2),
 \qquad y_{\rm rnd}^{\rm MP}(T)-y(T)=\delta_r v+O(\Delta t_r^2).
\]
Their norms are $\Delta t_r\left\|v\right\|/3+O(\Delta t_r^2)$, which proves both upper and lower first-order bounds. Since $N_r/3=2^r+1/3$, the crossing-step midpoint lies after the physical switch. Sampling therefore treats that whole step as post-switch, exactly as switching at its earlier node $\widetilde\theta_r$. The fitted estimate follows from \eqref{eq:fitmidtiming}. Finally all element fields and facet traces are constant-compatible, their spatial curls vanish, and $\mathbf{E}_{h,T}=\widehat{\mathbf{E}}_h$. Hence the HDG dissipation is zero and the HDG equations reduce exactly to \eqref{eq:sharpA}.

name: State convergence need not give uniform field convergence

title: Proof
body_md:
Bounded modal generators give the uniform continuous-state estimate by Proposition~\ref{prop:timing}. The constitutive law gives
\[
 \widetilde{\mathbf{E}}-\mathbf{E}
 =\frac{\widetilde{\mathbf{D}}-\mathbf{D}-\widetilde{s}(\widetilde{\mathbf{Q}}-\mathbf{Q})}{\epsilon_0}
  -\frac{(\widetilde{s}-s)\mathbf{Q}}{\epsilon_0}.
\]
The first term is $O(|\delta|)$. The second vanishes off the interval swept by the switch and has height approaching the constitutive jump on that interval. There,
\[
 \widetilde{\mathbf{E}}-\mathbf{E}
 =\pm\frac{s_+-s_-}{\epsilon_0}\mathbf{Q}(\theta)+O(|\delta|),
\]
where continuity and piecewise bounded derivatives of $\mathbf{Q}$ give a uniform remainder. Taking the essential supremum gives \eqref{eq:m2sup}; integrating the squared norm over the swept interval and adding the $O(\delta^2)$ contribution outside gives \eqref{eq:m2L2}. The argument for $\mathbf{P}$ uses its constitutive reconstruction.
